content: Transitioning from 'FREQUENCY SHIFT' (142 BPM) to 'Electric Universe' (145 BPM) worked well with a 45-second smooth blend. The slight energy bump (142 to 145) feels natural for a psytrance peak. Used a long blend to let the complex textures of both tracks overlap.

Transitioned from high-energy (9/10) peak-time psytrance (Music On - Holografic - Electric Universe) into a cinematic, mystical intro (3/10) of 'Goa Energy — Cosmic Dance'. Used a 45s do_bass_swap to manage the energy drop. The contrast between the relentless driving bass of the first track and the ethereal vocal chants of the second created a powerful 'reset' moment in the set. Phase-aligned the bass swap at a 32s phrase boundary to keep the rhythmic flow intact despite the energy shift.

When transitioning between different psytrance bass rhythms (e.g., triplet bass at 142 BPM to a rolling bassline), a do_bass_swap over 45-60s is superior to a standard blend. It prevents the 'muddy' low-end clash that occurs when two high-energy psytrance kicks overlap, even when beat-synced. Phase alignment (align_beats) is mandatory to ensure the rolling bass locks into the groove of the outgoing triplet.

When transitioning from a peak energy tribal acid track (energy 9) to a lower energy hypnotic psytrance track (energy 4), a 45-second do_bass_swap provides a much cleaner handoff than a standard blend. The bass swap preserves the rhythmic pulse while allowing the atmospheric elements of the new track to establish themselves without clashing with the high-intensity synths of the outgoing track.

Transitioned from a high-energy (8/10) Melodic Goa track with rolling triplets into a lower-energy (3/10) atmospheric Psytrance intro. Used a 45-second bass-swap to manage the energy drop. The contrast between the spoken-word purpose vocal of the outgoing track and the cinematic 'Ohm' textures of the incoming track created a deep, immersive shift. Note: Even with a 2:1 BPM sync (70 vs 140), aligning beats and using a long bass-swap keeps the psychedelic flow intact.

Transitioned from a high-energy (8/10) driving Psytrance track (Temple of Frequency XVIII) into a mystical, cinematic intro (3/10) of 'Midnight Raga'. Used a 60s bass-swap to allow the atmospheric Indian flute and tabla textures to bleed into the mechanical groove of the outgoing track. This 'energy-drop' transition works well for resetting the vibe before a new build.
